# A ball with a one-limb center from an interval given as two values of T

<!-- Generated by docs/tools/reference.py from gen/claims.json, gen/kernels/, include/kairn/gen/bounds.hpp, proofs/gen/, proofs/audit/, results/milestone2/brute/ and docs/tools/reference_operations.py. Do not edit: run python3 docs/tools/reference.py. -->

Kernel `ball_from_interval_1` · proved · [all operations](index.md) · [how to read this page](reading.md)

## What it computes

A ball $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, that contains the interval $[l_o, h_i]$ of two values of `T`; or the whole line, or the empty set:

$$Z \supseteq [l_o, h_i].$$

## C++

| Form | Operands | Result | Note |
|---|---|---|---|
| `from_interval(lo, hi)` | `T`, `T` | `Ball<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>::from_interval(lo, hi)`, the ball of `Interval<T, 1>(lo, hi)` in one kernel; the bounds are guarded ([rule R3](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)); `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |
| `from_bounds(lo, hi)` | `T`, `T` | `Ball<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>::from_bounds(lo, hi)`, the same ball as `from_interval(lo, hi)`, under the name `Interval` has too ([One enclosure interface](enclosure.md#the-interface)); the bounds are guarded ([rule R3](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)); `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |
| `from_bounds(lo, hi)` | `Expansion<T, 1>`, `Expansion<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>` | `Ball<T, 1>::from_bounds(lo, hi)`, the same ball as `from_interval(lo, hi)`, under the name `Interval` has too ([One enclosure interface](enclosure.md#the-interface)); the bounds are guarded ([rule R3](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)); `constexpr`; rounds, and is preceded by the debug build's check of the rounding mode |

`T` is `float` or `double`; the operations are in namespace `kairn`, header `kairn/kairn.hpp`. The operators and functions also accept the marker `kairn::unverified` on an operand, which they need while the kernel is UNVERIFIED.

## Requires

- $l_o$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.
- $h_i$ is any value of `T`: a number, $\pm\infty$ or a NaN.

## Guarantees

For operands that satisfy the requirements, finite, infinite or NaN:

- The result $Z$, of center $c_w$ and radius $r_w$, is a canonical ball.
- If a bound is a NaN, whatever the other, or both are the same infinity ($[+\infty, +\infty]$, $[-\infty, -\infty]$): $Z$ is the whole line (center 0, radius $+\infty$).
- Otherwise, if the bounds are reversed, $l_o > h_i$: $Z$ is the empty set (every limb a NaN).
- Otherwise, if both are finite ($l_o \le h_i$): $Z$ is a finite ball that contains $[l_o, h_i]$.
- Then $l_o \le c_w \le h_i$ and $\lvert c_w - \tfrac{l_o + h_i}{2}\rvert \le u\,\lvert \tfrac{l_o + h_i}{2}\rvert + \eta$, and $r_w = \mathrm{RU}(\max(c_w - l_o, h_i - c_w))$, the smallest radius of `T` for that center.
- Otherwise ($l_o \le h_i$, $l_o < +\infty$, $h_i > -\infty$, and a bound is infinite): $Z$ is the whole line; a ball cannot be a half-line.

Proved for every binary format with a precision of at least 2 bits, rounding to nearest with ties to even and with gradual underflow, in the IEEE model, with signed zeros, infinities, NaN and overflow. Both limb types qualify: `double` has 53 bits, `float` has 24 bits.

## Status

**Proved.** Rocq checks the theorem `ball_from_interval_1_correct`, in [`proofs/theories/IeeeBallSets.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/theories/IeeeBallSets.v); the audit of `make -C proofs` prints the axioms its proof depends on (`Print Assumptions ball_from_interval_1_correct`, in [`proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/gen/IeeeAudit.v)) and finds none beyond the four allowed ([Axioms](#axioms)).

## Axioms

The audit accepts a proof only if every axiom it depends on is one of the four listed in [`proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/proofs/audit/allowed_axioms.txt) ([Proofs](../proofs/index.md#the-four-axioms) says what each states):

- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_forall_dec`
- `ClassicalDedekindReals.sig_not_dec`
- `FunctionalExtensionality.functional_extensionality_dep`
- `Classical_Prop.classic`

Which of them the proof of `ball_from_interval_1_correct` depends on is not copied here: only a run of Rocq computes it. The CI prints it for every push to `main` and every pull request, and keeps what the audit printed as the artifact `proof-audit` of each run of the [Proofs workflow](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/actions/workflows/proofs.yml).

## Source

**Algorithm:** interval_make_1, then interval_to_ball_1, the special balls selected last (Milestone 2 listing; equal infinities the whole line, 2026-11-20). **License:** algorithm and proof: MIT.

## Listing

From [`gen/kernels/ball_from_interval_1.kernel`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/blob/main/gen/kernels/ball_from_interval_1.kernel), the description the C++ and the formal model (`proofs/gen/IeeeModel.v`) are generated from. Each line is one operation of `T`; one that rounds rounds to nearest, and `prod(a, b)` is $\mathrm{RN}(ab)$, written as a fused multiply-add with a zero addend ([the kernel IR](../developer/architecture.md#the-kernel-ir)).
It calls [`interval_to_ball_1`](interval_to_ball_1.md).

```
# A ball with a one-limb center from an interval [lo, hi] of two values of T supplied by the program
# (milestone2.md, "One enclosure interface", "A ball from an interval of two T"): the values of
# interval_make_1, which guards the bounds (rule R3), followed by interval_to_ball_1, as the page says
# of Ball<T, 1> from two T. So it has the three cases of ball_from_interval_2: a NaN bound, and two
# bounds that are the same infinity, [+inf, +inf] or [-inf, -inf], give the whole line through the
# whole-line interval (decided on 2026-11-20, as for interval_make_1: a value from the program that is
# not finite never makes the empty set); lo > hi (rv, false with a NaN) gives the empty ball through
# the empty interval, and only it; and an interval with an infinite bound the whole line; finite bounds
# lo <= hi give the ball of interval_to_ball_1: its center within u |m| + eta of the midpoint m and in
# [lo, hi], and the smallest radius of T for that center. The listing computes those values in
# another order: interval_to_ball_1 of the guarded bounds where interval_make_1 returns them (v), of
# [0, 0] otherwise, then, where v is false, the ball that interval_to_ball_1 makes of the empty
# interval (a NaN center and radius) where the bounds are reversed (rv), and of the whole line
# (center 0, radius +inf) otherwise. Where interval_make_1
# selects those intervals before the halving of interval_mid_rad_1, GCC 13 on x86-64 duplicates the
# halving on the path of a constant bound (3 fused multiply-adds for 2, which the object-code check
# refuses); selected after it, the products are computed once. [0, 0] rather than the bounds as they
# are: constant evaluation then computes nothing of a NaN bound (Clang refuses an operation whose
# result is a NaN, even of a NaN operand) nor of the empty interval (inf - inf), and gives the ball of
# every pair of bounds.

gl     = guard(lo)
gu     = guard(hi)
ok     = le(gl, gu)
nl     = lt(gl, const inf)
mi     = neg(const inf)
nu     = lt(mi, gu)
va     = and(ok, nl)
v      = and(va, nu)
rv     = lt(gu, gl)
tl     = select(v, gl, 0)
tu     = select(v, gu, 0)
(c, r) = interval_to_ball_1(tl, tu)
ec     = select(rv, const nan, 0)
er     = select(rv, const nan, const inf)
cw     = select(v, c, ec)
rw     = select(v, r, er)
```

## Measured

The latest brute-force runs, from the stored summaries in [`results/milestone2/brute/`](https://github.com/danielepanozzo/kairn/tree/main/results/milestone2/brute) ([the report](../developer/results/brute-milestone2.md#ball_from_interval_1)): the oracle judged, in exact arithmetic, the results of the compiled kernel (every compiler, scalar and packed code, every contraction setting) on random operands of `binary64` and `binary32`, and those of the generator's interpreter on every operand of small formats. A measurement, not a bound.
They judged the kernel in the extended domain, infinite and NaN operands included, as the oracle reads its statement in the IEEE model ([Claims of the non-finite layer](../developer/architecture.md#claims-of-the-non-finite-layer)).

| Run | Cases judged | Failed |
|---|---|---|
| `binary64` (`double`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| `binary32` (`float`), compiled: 90 runners on 3 machines | 103 500 000 | 0 |
| toy formats, every operand: 5 domains of 5 formats | 6 416 404 | 0 |

## Not claimed

- Anything for operands that do not satisfy the requirements.
- The sign of a zero limb, and which NaN a NaN result is: the claims compare neither.
